title: Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ 1–5 — The Prophets: the eschatological reckoning draws near

translation.sourceText: Arabic Qur'anic text from earliest-attested Hijazi-script manuscripts (Tübingen Ma VI 165 for Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ; Codex Parisino-petropolitanus for Sūrat al-Qamar and Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah); modern Cairo Hafs reference vocalization

verdicts.reasoning: Form VIII perfect *iqtaraba* correctly rendered 'has drawn near' — preserves the accomplished-near aspect against smoothing to 'is approaching' (future-progressive). *Ḥisāb* 'reckoning' as eschatological-audit lexically defensible. The Raëlian Age-of-Apocalypse pre-resolution disavowal is in place at the iqtaraba glossary entry; the Christian-supersessionist disavowal is verbatim ('typological-shared, not Christian-supersessionist pre-resolution'). Cross-corpus chain (Hebrew Bible *qārôb yôm YHWH* → NT *ēngiken*) correctly typologized as parallel-not-genetic. Surface English defensible against an Asad/Arberry/Pickthall comparator.

citations: Madelung 1974 'Origins of the Controversy concerning the Creation of the Koran' on the Miḥna khalq al-Qurʾān dispute
van Ess 1991-1997 Theologie und Gesellschaft on early Islamic theology
Asad 1980 / Pickthall 1930 register comparator
verdicts.reasoning: *Muḥdaṯ* rendered 'newly-given' is theologically neutral as claimed — does not pre-resolve between the Muʿtazila *khalq al-Qurʾān* ('newly-created') and the Ashʿarī ('eternally-existing-but-revealed-in-time') readings. The Miḥna controversy is correctly anchored to al-Maʾmūn 833 CE / al-Mutawakkil 846 CE reversal. *Ḏikr* preserved as 'reminder' (Asad/Arberry consensus). Cross-corpus to Hebrew *zēker* / Aramaic *dukrān* documented as Semitic-cognate, not collapsed. *Yalʿabūn* 'at play' literal-philological.

citations: Asad 1980 ad loc.
Pickthall 1930 ad loc.
Mark 6:3 / John 1:14 sarx / Heb 2:14 cross-corpus mortal-prophet topos
verdicts.reasoning: *Bašar* rendered 'a mortal like you' preserves the Quranic mortal-vs-angelic anthropology. *Najwā* 'whispered counsel' accurate. *Siḥr* 'sorcery' renders the polemical-accusation category cleanly. Cross-corpus chain to the Beelzebul-accusation (Mark 3:22-30 / Matt 12:22-32) and Hebrew *kešep̄* (Exod 22:18 / Deut 18:10-11) typologized correctly as parallel-classification structure, not 'Quranic siḥr = Hebrew kešep̄.' No Christological pre-resolution of the mortal-prophet topos. *A-fa-taʾtūna s-siḥra wa-antum tubṣirūn* 'will you then approach sorcery with open eyes' preserves the *fa* rhetorical-coordination.

verdicts.reasoning: *As-Samīʿ al-ʿAlīm* 'the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing' is the standard Anglophone-Quranic-translation rendering (Asad/Pickthall consensus). The 32-occurrence frequency for the pair is correct. *Samāwāt wa-l-arḍ* 'heavens and earth' merism cross-corpus to Gen 1:1 documented as typological-Near-Eastern creation-totality, not as 'identical phrase.' Gimaret 1988 correctly named as foundational modern study of the divine-names framework.

citations: Goldziher 1896 Abhandlungen zur arabischen Philologie on the pre-Islamic mantic-poet
Stetkevych 1993 The Mute Immortals Speak on the šāʿir as oracular-spokesman with jinnī-inspiration
Neuwirth 2014 on the Qurʾān's polemical rejection of the kāhin / šāʿir / majnūn category
verdicts.reasoning: The *šāʿir* 'poet-seer' rendering is the chapter's most distinctive translation decision and is defensible: the pre-Islamic Arabian *šāʿir* is the mantic-poet with attendant *jinnī*, not the modern lyric-poet. The bare-'poet' rendering (Asad/Pickthall) is lexically anachronistic. The compound 'poet-seer' preserves the polemical-classification force that pairs the *šāʿir* with the *kāhin* (37:36 majnūn šāʿir) and *majnūn* (52:30, 69:41). *Aḍġāṯu aḥlām* 'jumble of dreams' lexically accurate. *Āya* 'sign' preserves the multi-valent Quranic technical force (sign/miracle/verse) without pre-resolving to NT *sēmeion*. *Al-awwalūn* 'the ancients' standard. Cross-corpus chain to Matt 12:38-42 / John 6:30 / 1 Cor 1:22 sign-demand documented as parallel-prophetic-rhetoric, not 'these prophets are the same.'

paragraphs.rasm: اقترب للناس حسابهم وهم في غفله معرضون
paragraphs.text: ٱقْتَرَبَ لِلنَّاسِ حِسَابُهُمْ وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مُّعْرِضُونَ
paragraphs.translit: iqtaraba li-n-nāsi ḥisābuhum wa-hum fī ġaflatin muʿriḍūna

i18n.en: The reckoning has drawn near for humankind, yet they, in heedlessness, are turning away.

notes.official: Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ opens with the Form VIII perfect verb *iqtaraba* 'has drawn near' — one of only two suras in the Qur'an (with Sūrat al-Qamar 54:1) to open with this verb (Ṭabarī, Zamakhsharī, Rāzī foreground the structural-stylistic parallel; both openings announce eschatological imminence). The phrase sits within a broader Near-Eastern apocalyptic-imminence tradition (Hebrew Bible *qārôb yôm YHWH* at Joel 1:15, Isa 13:6, Zeph 1:7, 1:14; NT *ēngiken hē basileia tōn ouranōn* at Mark 1:15, Matt 3:2; the parousia-imminence tradition at 1 Thess 5; 2 Pet 3) — preserved as cross-corpus typology, not endorsed as Christian-supersessionist pre-resolution of the Quranic eschatology. The Raëlian canon engages this ayah in *Extra-Terrestrials Took Me To Their Planet* as a marker of the impending Elohim-return / Age-of-Apocalypse; the WoH-Translation acknowledges the citation without endorsing the canon's pre-filtered eschatological reading (per the *parasangs* acknowledgment-without-endorsement precedent at SHQM-WOH-1:31).

paragraphs.rasm: ما ياتيهم من ذكر من ربهم محدث الا استمعوه وهم يلعبون
paragraphs.text: مَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِم مُّحْدَثٍ إِلَّا ٱسْتَمَعُوهُ وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ
paragraphs.translit: mā yaʾtīhim min ḏikrin min rabbihim muḥdaṯin illā stamaʿūhu wa-hum yalʿabūna

i18n.en: No newly-given reminder comes to them from their Lord but they listen to it while they are at play,

notes.official: Two technical-Quranic terms appear together: *ḏikr* 'reminder' (one of the Qur'an's distinctive self-designations, cf. Sura 15:9, 21:50, 38:1, 50:1; cross-corpus to Hebrew *zēker* / *zikkārôn* at Exod 3:15, Hos 12:5, Ps 30:5 and to Aramaic *dukrān*) and *muḥdaṯ* 'newly-given' (the lexical anchor of the famous *khalq al-Qurʾān* 'createdness of the Qur'an' controversy under the Miḥna of al-Maʾmūn, 827-848 CE). The 'newly-given' rendering preserves theological neutrality — neither the Muʿtazila 'newly-created' position nor the Ashʿarī 'eternally-existing-but-newly-revealed-in-time' position is pre-resolved (Madelung 1974; van Ess 1991-1997). The opponents' *yalʿabūn* 'they are at play' charge fits the broader Quranic polemical-rejection-pattern documented at the al-anbiya entry.

paragraphs.rasm: لاهيه قلوبهم واسروا النجوى الذين ظلموا هل هذا الا بشر مثلكم افتاتون السحر وانتم تبصرون
paragraphs.text: لَاهِيَةً قُلُوبُهُمْ ۗ وَأَسَرُّوا۟ ٱلنَّجْوَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ هَلْ هَٰذَا إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ ۖ أَفَتَأْتُونَ ٱلسِّحْرَ وَأَنتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ
paragraphs.translit: lāhiyatan qulūbuhum, wa-asarrū n-najwā lladīna ẓalamū, hal hāḏā illā bašarun miṯlukum, a-fa-taʾtūna s-siḥra wa-antum tubṣirūna

i18n.en: their hearts distracted. And those who do wrong have hidden their whispered counsel: "Is this anything but a mortal like you? Will you then approach sorcery with open eyes?"

notes.official: Two opponents-of-the-prophets polemical categories land in one ayah. *Bašar* 'a mortal like you' is the distinctive Quranic-anthropological insistence that prophets are mortal-human, not angelic (a pattern repeated at Sura 17:93-94; 18:110; 23:24; 25:7; 41:6; cross-corpus to Mark 6:3 'is not this the carpenter?'; John 1:14 *sarx*; Heb 2:14 'flesh and blood'). *Siḥr* 'sorcery' is the standard polemical-accusation category, paired across the Qur'an with *kāhin* / *šāʿir* / *majnūn* (cross-corpus to Hebrew *kešep̄* at Exod 22:18 / Deut 18:10-11; NT Beelzebul-accusation at Mark 3:22-30 / Matt 12:22-32). The opponents' classification structure is preserved as a polemical-rhetorical pattern, not adjudicated.

paragraphs.rasm: قال ربي يعلم القول في السماء والارض وهو السميع العليم
paragraphs.text: قَالَ رَبِّي يَعْلَمُ ٱلْقَوْلَ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۖ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
paragraphs.translit: qāla rabbī yaʿlamu l-qawla fī s-samāʾi wa-l-arḍi, wa-huwa s-samīʿu l-ʿalīmu

i18n.en: He said: "My Lord knows every word in the heavens and the earth, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."

notes.official: The ayah closes with the divine-epithet pair *as-Samīʿ al-ʿAlīm* 'the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing' — one of the most frequent pairs in the Qur'an (32 occurrences), part of the *asmāʾ al-ḥusnā* 'most beautiful names' framework (Sura 7:180; 17:110; 20:8; 59:24). Cross-corpus to the Hebrew Bible El-compound and YHWH-epithet traditions (El Shaddai, YHWH Tzeva'ot, *ʾēl raḥûm wĕ-ḥannûn*) flagged as typological-shared-Near-Eastern divine-epithet form, not 'these epithets ARE the Hebrew divine names.' Gimaret 1988 *Les noms divins en Islam* is the foundational modern study.

paragraphs.rasm: بل قالوا اضغث احلام بل افترىه بل هو شاعر فلياتنا بايه كما ارسل الاولون
paragraphs.text: بَلْ قَالُوٓا۟ أَضْغَٰثُ أَحْلَٰمٍۭ بَلِ ٱفْتَرَىٰهُ بَلْ هُوَ شَاعِرٌ فَلْيَأْتِنَا بِـَٔايَةٍ كَمَآ أُرْسِلَ ٱلْأَوَّلُونَ
paragraphs.translit: bal qālū aḍġāṯu aḥlāmin bali ftarāhu bal huwa šāʿirun fa-l-yaʾtinā bi-āyatin kamā ursila l-awwalūna

i18n.en: But they say: "A jumble of dreams! No, he has forged it! No, he is a poet-seer! Let him then bring us a sign, as the ancients were sent."

notes.official: The *šāʿir* crux is the Editor's most-contested rendering decision in this chapter. The pre-Islamic Arabian *šāʿir* is the inspired-mantic-poet / diviner-seer with attendant *jinnī*-inspiration, NOT the modern lyric-poet category (Goldziher 1896 *Abhandlungen zur arabischen Philologie*; Stetkevych 1993 *The Mute Immortals Speak*; Neuwirth 2014; Bauer 2010). Rendering as plain 'poet' (Asad/Pickthall) is lexically anachronistic and obscures the polemical-classification force — the opponents are categorizing Muḥammad alongside the *kuhhān* 'soothsayers', the *šuʿarāʾ* 'inspired-poets', and the *majnūn* 'jinn-possessed' (Sura 36:69; 37:36; 52:30; 69:41). The 'poet-seer' compound preserves the pre-classical mantic category. *Aya* 'sign' carries the multi-valent Quranic technical force (sign / miracle / verse); cross-corpus to Hebrew *ʾôt* and NT *sēmeion* flagged as typological-shared-Near-Eastern prophetic-sign tradition.
